record_identity.title: Singapore finance director transferred over US$499,000 after deepfake executive video call

incident_identity.date_basis: Date follows the reviewed registry or primary occurrence record; no narrower time is inferred.

summary: A finance director at a multinational corporation was contacted by scammers impersonating senior company personnel and joined a Zoom video conference in which the company's chief executive officer and others were impersonated using deepfake technology. The victim transferred more than US$499,000 from the company's bank account. Singapore and Hong Kong police later traced and withheld the funds after the victim discovered the scam.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: A finance director at a multinational corporation was contacted by scammers impersonating senior company personnel and joined a Zoom video conference in which the company's chief executive officer and others were impersonated using deepfake technology. The victim transferred more than US$499,000 from the company's bank account. Singapore and Hong Kong police later traced and withheld the funds after the victim discovered the scam.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Human scammers used deepfake video to impersonate senior company personnel during a live call and created false executive authority for a transfer exceeding US$499,000. Police evidence establishes the transfer and later recovery. The scam objective belongs to the human operators, not the synthetic media system.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: High-value payment controls must authenticate the transaction and the authority behind it through an independent channel, not only the apparent face and voice of senior personnel. Recovery after transfer is valuable but cannot substitute for approval procedures resilient to real-time impersonation.
assessment_boundaries: The record relies on the reported police account and does not identify the victim company or every participant in the call.
The evidence does not establish which tools or models produced the synthetic media.
More than US$499,000 was transferred before police traced and withheld the funds; ultimate unrecovered loss is not asserted.
The occurrence does not establish negligence or legal liability by the victim or service providers.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Audiovisual executive presence must not be fabricated to create payment authority; consequential instructions require independent authentication of the represented principals.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The synthetic executives supplied the materially false corporate authority context on which the victim relied when transferring funds, while police evidence later supported recovery.
Deepfake executives in a Zoom meeting supplied false senior authority to the finance director, who transferred more than US$499,000.
